# trend.sst

Daily sea surface temperature aggregated to a global S2 discrete grid
(level 5, ~290 km cells) as *sufficient statistics*: per (cell, date) we
store `n` (valid pixels), `sumw` (summed cos-latitude weights), `sumwx`,
and `sumwx2`. Sums are associative, so any union of cells over any dates
aggregates exactly: every region is a cell selection, every mean,
variance, or hierarchical rollup is arithmetic on the sums. No geometry
happens at daily-run time; all of it lives in a one-off pixel-to-cell
mapping per source grid.

Sources: OISST v2.1 (0.25 degree, 1981-09 onward) and GHRSST MUR
(0.01 degree, 2002-06 onward). Same schema, same registry, never pooled
(`sums/oisst/`, `sums/ghrsst/`).

Design notes that the code depends on:

* S2 cell ids cross the R boundary as **character tokens**, never bare
  `s2_cell` doubles: NaN-payload ids (top of face 3, i.e. the Pacific)
  collapse under base double semantics in `duplicated()`, `match()`,
  `%in%`. Same-level tokens share a length so character sort equals id
  sort.
* The mapping is **dense and positional**: element i of a band read is
  pixel i, nothing stores pixel identity. `meta.rds` stamps the grid
  signature and `check_mapping()` hard-stops on mismatch.
* NA pixels contribute nothing via the `fin` guard, so the dense mapping
  is correct without culling; culling is a later optimization, not a
  correctness feature.

## Task map

Each step is small and checkable; run in order, OISST first (the whole
OISST path takes minutes and exercises every code path GHRSST will use).

### 0. Repo hygiene

- [ ] `devtools::load_all()` runs clean
- [ ] `data-raw/oisstfiles.R`: rebuild the catalog **without projwin**
      (full grid is the product) -> `oisstfiles.parquet`

### 1. Registry (once, source-independent)

- [ ] `registry <- build_registry(5L)`; expect 6144 rows
- [ ] `arrow::write_parquet(registry, "s2_registry.parquet")`
- [ ] sanity: `anyDuplicated(registry$cell) == 0`,
      `all(diff(order(registry$cell)) == 1)` (already sorted)

### 2. OISST mapping (seconds)

- [ ] `src <- oisst_source("oisstfiles.parquet")`; check
      `src$grid$dimension` is 1440 x 720 and extent is 0..360, -90..90
- [ ] `build_mapping(src, registry, band_rows = 720L)`
- [ ] `check_mapping(src)` passes

### 3. One-date end-to-end check (the important gate)

- [ ] `accumulate_date(src$files$dsn[i], src$files$date[i], src, registry)`
      for one recent date
- [ ] read the parquet back: values sane (Celsius range, land absent)
- [ ] **cross-check**: `sum(sumwx)/sum(sumw)` over all cells equals a
      directly computed cos-weighted global mean of the same file
      (xarray or tidync one-liner) to several decimals
- [ ] orientation check: pick one cell token near a known feature
      (e.g. equatorial cold tongue), confirm its mean is plausible --
      guards against a silent north/south flip

### 4. OISST backfill (minutes to an hour, resumable)

- [ ] run `data-raw/backfill_oisst.R`; rerun-to-resume semantics, FAIL
      dates just retry next run
- [ ] gap check on completion: `diff(sort(unique(date)))` in the sums

### 5. First science: the ClimateReanalyzer reproduction

- [ ] `cells_latband(registry, -60, 60)` -> `series_stats()` -> plot
- [ ] `validate/compare_cr.R`: cell series vs bracket (straddling ring
      in/out) vs pixel-exact projwin clip on ~200 sampled dates
- [ ] expectations to test: exact value inside the bracket; cell-minus-
      exact small (order 0.01-0.05 C), **stationary** (no trend), with a
      seasonal wiggle. This figure is the quantitative license for
      preferring generic cells over bespoke clips.

### 6. GHRSST on Setonix

- [ ] `ghrsst_source()`; grid check 36000 x 17999
- [ ] `build_mapping(src, registry, band_rows = 512L)` -- bands align to
      COG tile rows; ~8 GB dense uncompressed, use `compress = "gzip"`
      in saveRDS if scratch quota is tight
- [ ] missing-pixel constancy test (sample dates across seasons/eras,
      compare `is.finite` patterns) -- informs the optional cull, does
      not block anything
- [ ] backfill runner: `accumulate_date` over dates with mirai daemons
      (few fat workers, each looping bands within its date; a whole date
      is ~5 GB so 96 whole-date workers will not fit), sbatch wrapper as
      per the warp pipeline
- [ ] known-bad dates from the warp series (2025-08-24..29 input-starved
      analysis, 2003-11 pair) should reappear here; leave them in the
      sums, flag at query time

### 7. Downstream (in any order)

- [ ] OISST vs GHRSST product comparison over the 2002+ overlap: join on
      (cell, date) -- arguably the most novel output of the framework
- [ ] Pacific series re-derived as a cell selection (retire the NE-mask
      warp pipeline or keep as another validation oracle)
- [ ] per-cell trend/anomaly maps from `cell_means()` baselines
- [ ] analysis-quality trace: spatial roughness per date to detect
      input-starved analyses (needs a fifth statistic; schema additions
      are cheap while the record is one rerun away)

## Layout

```
R/                 cells.R sources.R mapping.R accumulate.R series.R
data-raw/          oisstfiles.R backfill_oisst.R
validate/          compare_cr.R   (the old warp trick, demoted to oracle)
s2_registry.parquet
mapping/<source>/  band_%04i.rds + meta.rds   (not in git for ghrsst)
sums/<source>/     YYYY-MM-DD.parquet         (the product; on Acacia)
```
